Mini-course for teachers

[Don’t] call me “Miss”

A course about the new era of teaching, drawn from my own experience. For teachers of more than just Swedish, and of more than just languages.

Who it’s for

This course is for you if you teach

Whatever your subject, level or format – this course is about how to teach in the new era: from methodology to psychology, brand and sales.

🧑‍🏫

Any subject

The course isn’t tied to Swedish or to languages in general – its main focus is teaching as a whole.

📈

Wanting to grow

If it feels like you’ve been standing still for months, even though you sense the need to move forward.

🌱

Wanting a fresh start

If you feel the old model of teaching no longer works – and you want to find your own, including how to cope with self-doubt.

What I bring

My experience and my mistakes

The course isn’t built on theory but on what I went through myself over my years of teaching – including what I would do differently.

1

Years of language-teaching practice

Experience gathered not only from teaching Swedish but from teaching languages in general – and from what keeps coming up, whatever the language.

2

An honest look at my own mistakes

I share precisely the things that didn’t work or cost me time and energy – so that you can avoid them.

3

A system I spent years looking for myself

Methodology, brand, sales and how to work with self-doubt – including impostor syndrome – I gathered all of this for myself, and now I’m sharing what I’ve collected.

Programme

Course programme

Seven modules with theory and practice.

MODULE 1. A new-generation teacher

Topics:
  • why the old model of teaching is dying
  • why “knowing the language well” ≠ being able to teach
  • the psychology of the modern learner
  • how people really learn languages in 2026
  • what a safe learning environment is
  • your role: teacher / mentor / creator / guide
Practice:
  • shaping your own teaching philosophy

MODULE 2. Methodology that doesn’t put people to sleep

Topics:
  • how to explain difficult things simply
  • lessons without boring exercises
  • a speaking-first system
  • how to create “lively” lessons
  • a lesson structure where the brain actually retains information
  • how memory and repetition work
  • how to use memes, reels, AI, TV series and TikTok
  • how to adapt a lesson for:
    • ADHD
    • introverts
    • children
    • adults
    • people studying after work
Practice:
  • creating your own lesson
  • redesigning a “school-style” lesson into a modern one

MODULE 3. The teacher’s psychology

Topics:
  • impostor syndrome
  • fear of speaking on camera
  • fear of charging high prices
  • the teacher’s emotional labour
  • how not to burn out
  • boundaries with students
  • the “rescuer syndrome”
  • why teachers work 12-hour days and stay poor
Practice:
  • an energy map
  • a recovery system
  • anti-burnout routine

MODULE 4. The teacher’s brand

Topics:
  • how a teacher can blog without the cringe
  • content that sells without saying “buy my course”
  • reels for teachers
  • storytelling
  • positioning
  • how to stop being “just another tutor”
  • visuals
  • tone of voice
  • how to build an audience that trusts you
Practice:
  • creating a bio, a content strategy, 30 reel ideas and a series of stories

MODULE 5. Selling without being salesy

Topics:
  • a trial lesson that converts
  • how not to “hard-sell”
  • selling through trust
  • soft sales
  • how to talk about price
  • how to stop being afraid of raising your prices
  • a package system
  • premium positioning
Practice:
  • scripts for the trial lesson, text messages, voice messages and selling the course

MODULE 6. The teacher’s system

Topics:
  • Notion for teachers
  • a materials database
  • AI for lessons
  • automation
  • how not to spend 3 hours preparing for a lesson
  • reusable content
  • a filing system
  • templates
Practice:
  • a ready-made teacher operating system

MODULE 7. Impostor syndrome

Topics:
  • what impostor syndrome is – and what it isn’t
  • the five faces of the impostor in teaching
  • “I’m not a native speaker” – language teachers’ fear
  • “what if a student asks something I don’t know?”
  • the impostor in pricing, content and launches
  • comparison and social media
  • tools: how to live with the impostor’s voice
Practice:
  • a folder of evidence
  • a 14-day diary of impostor thoughts
  • my “good enough” standard
  • a letter to your beginner self
  • 30 days of small brave actions

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Is it right for me if I don’t teach a language?

Yes. The course isn’t tied to Swedish or to languages in general – it’s about teaching as a whole: methodology, the teacher’s psychology, brand, sales and a system for your work. My own experience is in language teaching, so some of the examples may be about languages, but the approach and the tools work for any subject.

How long will it take?

The course has seven modules – the plan is one module a week, so seven weeks. But you go at your own pace. To make it easier, the bonus PDF includes a ready-made plan for completing the course in 7 weeks.

How is VIP different?

The “Course + personal review” plan includes everything the “Course” plan does, plus a personal 45-minute online meeting with me: a review of your trial lesson, Instagram or prices.

How do I buy it?

Choose a plan above and click the button below it. If anything is unclear, or you’d rather write to me, email me at fika.med.maria@gmail.com.
